 Magnitude 5.7 quake jolts Kumamoto Prefecture, but no tsunami warning issued
 A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture and nearby areas at around 2:22 a.m. Thursday. No tsunami warning was issued. 
 | Japan Meteorological Agency

 Nov 19, 2026 
 A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture and nearby areas early Thursday, but no tsunami warning was issued.
 The temblor, which occurred at around 2:22 a.m. at a depth of about 10 kilometers in the Amakusa-Ashikita region of the prefecture, measured up to lower shindo  5, the fifth-highest level on the nation’s seismic intensity scale, the Japan Meteorological Agency said. 
 Lower 5 was registered in the city of Minamata in Kumamoto, while the Kumamoto city of Yatsushiro, the city of Miyazaki, the capital of neighboring Miyazaki Prefecture, and the city of Izumi in Kagoshima Prefecture, also adjacent to Kumamoto, logged 4, the sixth-highest level.
 A series of aftershocks with an intensity of 1 or higher occurred following the 5.7 magnitude quake, which caused no tsunami, according to the agency.
 The agency urged people in areas that experienced strong shaking to be alert for quakes of up to around lower 5 or more powerful temblors for about a week.
 The 5.7 magnitude quake is believed to have occurred as a fault in the crust moved sideways and is thought to be part of seismic activities associated with a massive earthquake that hit Kumamoto on July 28. The July quake measured up to 7, the highest level on the Japanese scale.
